acceptanceCriteria: ALGORITHMS.md states the stage and precedence for unresolved hunk basis, missing criterion link, duplicated unknown link IDs and duplicated artifacts.
Native and portable consumers return the same stage and code for each of the four mutations, proven by a shared sealed case or paired tests in internal/cem/verify and interop/cem01-go.
Existing sealed S0E cases and protocol/cem-1.0/maps results are unchanged.
body: Found 2026-10-12 by the independent review of V1-1263 (branch claude/v1-1263-neutral-criterion from origin/main 19779517f) and confirmed by reading both consumers; runtime reproduction NOT_RUN. The native stable consumer (internal/cem/wire/stable.go ParseStable + validateStableGraph) and the portable consumer (interop/cem01-go/cem.go decodeStable + validateStableReferences) return different stage/code pairs for four cem/1.0 map mutations that no sealed S0E case covers. They predate V1-1263 and affect Tasks-form and plain-form maps alike. (1) A hunk basis entry naming an evidence ID that is not in change.evidence: native refuses at stage wire via validateReferences (stable.go ~line 139, code invalid-field); portable refuses at stage references with unresolved-reference (cem.go ~line 4017). (2) A map whose criterion has no criterionLinks entry: native returns reference-coherence from the usedCriteria/ids count (stable.go ~line 399); portable returns unresolved-reference from the linkedCriteria/criteria count (cem.go ~line 4001). (3) A link whose hunkIds repeats an unknown ID: native checks each ID for existence as it walks and returns unresolved-reference first (stable.go ~line 363); portable completes the duplicate scan first and returns duplicate-reference (cem.go ~line 3975). (4) A duplicated artifact path or digest: native returns duplicate-reference (stable.go ~line 428); portable returns artifact-role-closure (cem.go ~line 4047). Expected: CEM-V1-083 and the stable contract require identical results from both consumers for the same inputs. Actual: four divergent refusal codes. Fix: decide the canonical stage and precedence per case in protocol/cem-1.0/stable/ALGORITHMS.md, align the consumer that deviates, and add the four mutations as sealed refusal cases (a public case under protocol/cem-1.0/stable/ or S0E via tools/cem-stable-regen) so parity is tested rather than assumed. Interop cem01-go/stable_neutral_test.go only mutates the criterion and its link ID.

knowHow.text: 2026-10-12 V1-1265 review: verdictSha256 (CEM-V1-066) hashes the refusal code, so the native reference-coherence vs portable unresolved-reference divergence now yields different verdict digests for the same map (criterionLinks: [] on the public neutral-criterion map). Resolution must add a parity case asserting equal digests.

title: cem/1.0 consumers diverge on four refusal codes: hunk-basis stage, missing link, duplicated unknown link IDs, duplicated artifacts
